newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi says EMU delay bad for Europe and Italy.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi says EMU delay bad for Europe and Italy.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Tuesday any delay to the launch of a planned single currency would be bad for Europe and for Italy.

"The government has realised from the outset that it is in the interests of our country to take part in creating a single currency and that any suggestion of a postponement is against the interests of Europe and of Italy," he said in a statement.
Ciampi reiterated that Italy will convert its public debt into the planned single currency, the euro, from January 1, 1999, the date on which economic and monetary union (EMU) is due for launch.
"This will favour the creation of a critical mass in euros on the markets which will give assurances and will increase the credibility of the system," he said.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi has staked his political career on getting Italy to qualify for EMU at the outset and has pushed through nearly 100 trillion lire ($59 billion) of deficit-cutting measures since he took office in May last year to try to ensure that Italy's public finances are in order.
Prodi told a talk show on Monday night that any delay to EMU could prove fatal to the whole project.
"If we postpone it, it will not go ahead," he said. "Delay means losing faith."
Fears have been raised that EMU cfould be delayed or undermined because two major players -- France and Germany -- face political problems.

Germany is stuck in a row with the Bundesbank opposed to the Bonn government's plan to revalue its gold reserves to help achieve the EMU criteria, while a new French left government faces "cohabiting" with conservative President Jacques Chirac. ($1=1,695 lire)
